records.subject: Need to establish a Pilgrimage Department for the comprehensive development of major pilgrimage sites.
records.SM_Text:
Dr. Anil Sukhdeorao Bonde:

मै भारत के प्रमुख तीर्थ स्थलों के संरक्षण और सर्वांगीण विकास के लिए एक समर्पित संस्थागत व्यवस्था की आवश्यकता की ओरसरकार का ध्यान आकर्षित करना चाहता हूँ। भारत गहरी आस्था, आध्यात्मिकता और समृद्ध सांस्कृतिक परंपराओं की भूमि है। हर साल, करोड़ों श्रद्धालु दर्शन और पूजा-अर्चना के लिए मंदिरों, पवित्र नदियों, घाटों और अन्य पूजनीय स्थलों की यात्रा करते हैं। विभिन्न अध्ययनों से पता चलता है कि लगभग 55 प्रतिशत हिंदू आबादी हर साल धार्मिक तीर्थयात्रा करती है, जिससे ये स्थल न केवल आध्यात्मिक रूप से, बल्कि सामाजिक और आर्थिक रूप से भी महत्वपूर्ण हो जाते हैं। हालाँकि, कई तीर्थ केंद्रों में अभी भी पर्याप्त बुनियादी सुविधाओं का अभाव है। श्रद्धालुओं को अक्सर पीने के पानी, ठहरने की व्यवस्था, पार्किंग, परिवहन संपर्क, स्वास्थ्य सेवा और सुरक्षा व्यवस्था से जुड़ी चुनौतियों का सामना करना पड़ता है। कई जगहों पर नदियों और घाटों की स्वच्छता बनाए रखना और आसपास के प्राकृतिक पर्यावरण की रक्षा करना भी बड़ी चिंता का विषय है। इसके अलावा, कुछ तीर्थ क्षेत्रों के आसपास नशीले पदार्थों का सेवन, अवैध गतिविधियां और असामाजिक तत्वों की मौजूदगी उनकी पवित्रता को कम करती है और श्रद्धालुओं की भावनाओं को आहत करती है।

     मैं सरकार से आग्रह करता हूँ कि वह केंद्र में एक अलग तीर्थयात्रा विभाग स्थापित करने पर विचार करे, जिसका काम विकास योजनाएं तैयार करना, सुविधाओं सुधारना, पर्यावरण संरक्षण  करना, सुरक्षा को मजबूत करना और तीर्थ पर्यटन को बढ़ावा देना हो। ऐसा कदम श्रद्धालुओं के लिए सुविधाओं को बेहतर बनाएगा, स्थानीय रोजगार पैदा करेगा और भारत की पवित्र विरासत को संरक्षित करेगा। 

(ENDS)

records.subject: Need for policy to combat Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR).
records.SM_Text:
Dr. Anil SukhdeoraoBonde:

 I seek to bring to the attention of the Government, the growing threat of Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR), a silent pandemic that is weakening our ability to treat common infections and threatening the very foundation of modern medicine. India is among the world?s highest consumers of antibiotics. Misuse and overuse in both humans and animals, over-the-counter access, and poor waste management have made many infections harder and more expensive to treat. In 2021, India recorded an estimated 267,000 deaths directly attributable to AMR, with nearly a million associated deaths, ranking 57th globally in AMR mortality This growing resistance means longer hospital stays, higher treatment costs, and increased mortality, particularly among older adults. It also poses a serious risk to surgeries, cancer therapies, and intensive care, where effective antibiotics are essential. While India has launched the National Action Plan on AMR 2.0, challenges remain: poor surveillance, weak cross-sector coordination, unchecked antibiotic use in agriculture and animal husbandry, and inadequate public awareness

          I urge the Government to ensure implementation of NAP-AMR 2.0 with dedicated funding, strict regulation of antibiotic sales, and public education campaigns. We must treat antibiotics as a shared national resource not as routine consumer goods.  Timely action on AMR is not just a health necessity it is a national development imperative.

(ENDS)

records.subject: Need to recognize Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1) under the National Policy for Rare Diseases.
records.SM_Text:
Dr. Anil Sukhdeorao Bonde:

??????????? I draw attention of the Government to the need for formal recognition and systematic care for patients with Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1), a rare and complex genetic condition affecting approximately 1 in 3,000 to 5,000 people. NF1 often begins in childhood and causes tumours, bone abnormalities, learning disabilities and, in many cases, plexiform neurofibromas (PN) progressive nerve sheath tumours that can lead to pain, disfigurement and life-threatening complications. The psychosocial impact is profound, with patients facing stigma, bullying, isolation and deep emotional distress.? Despite this, NF1 remains under-recognised in India?s health policy, including the National Policy for Rare Diseases (NPRD). This lack of recognition restricts access to multidisciplinary care, innovative therapies, financial assistance, and structured rehabilitation.? Current disability assessment frameworks also fail to capture the invisible and fluctuating impairments caused by NF1.

??????????? Scientific progress now offers effective, targeted therapies for inoperable PN. Yet, without NPRD inclusion, such treatments remain inaccessible for most Indian patients.

??????????? I urge the Government to formally include NF1 under the NPRD to enable standardized care at Centres of Excellence, treatment funding, structured referrals, patient registries and advocacy support. This is a public health and moral imperative.

(ENDS)

records.subject: Need to recognize Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1) under the National Policy for Rare Diseases.
records.SM_Text:
Dr. Anil SukhdeoraoBonde: I draw attention of the Government to the need for formal recognition and systematic care for patients with Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1),a rare and complex genetic condition affecting approximately 1 in 3,000 to 5,000 people.NF1 often begins in childhood and causes tumours, bone abnormalities, learning disabilities and, in many cases, plexiform neurofibromas (PN)progressive nerve sheath tumours that can lead to pain, disfigurement and life-threatening complications. The psychosocial impact is profound, with patients facing stigma, bullying, isolation and deep emotional distress.Despite this, NF1 remains under-recognised in India?s health policy, including the National Policy for Rare Diseases (NPRD). This lack of recognition restricts access to multidisciplinary care, innovative therapies, financial assistance, and structured rehabilitation.Current disability assessment frameworks also fail to capture the invisible and fluctuating impairments caused by NF1. Scientific progress now offers effective, targeted therapies for inoperable PN. Yet, without NPRD inclusion, such treatments remain inaccessible for most Indian patients. I urge the Government to formally include NF1 under the NPRD to enable standardized care at Centres of Excellence, treatment funding, structured referrals, patient registries and advocacy support. This is a public health and moral imperative.

(ENDS)

records.subject: Need for a Dedicated National Response for Type 1 Diabetes in India.
records.SM_Text:
Dr. Anil Sukhdeorao Bonde: There is an urgent need for a dedicated national framework to support children and young adults living with Type 1 Diabetes, a lifelong autoimmune condition that strikes early and demands daily insulin and vigilant care. Unlike Type 2 diabetes, Type 1 is not lifestyle-related and cannot be prevented.? It requires round-the-clock access to insulin, glucometers, ketone strips, trained providers, and school safety protocols. India has over 1 million people living with Type 1 Diabetes, yet their needs are not fully integrated into public health programmes. ?Since they do not fall under the ?rare? disease category and are relatively small in number, they are often overlooked in NCD (Non-Communicable Diseases) programmes. Meeting their needs is neither complex nor unaffordable. India already manufactures world-class insulin used globally, I, therefore, urge the Government to: 1.???? Create a national Type 1 Diabetes pathway with dedicated budgets. 2.??????????? Ensure uninterrupted access to insulin and monitoring tools across public facilities.3.??????? Mandate school safety protocols for hypoglycaemia management.4. Strengthen device regulation and data systems for better care outcomes. Type 1 Diabetes care is an opportunity to save lives, uphold health equity, and make India a global leader in compassionate, high-quality diabetes care.

(ENDS)

records.subject: Demand to adopt research-linked incentives for Med-Tech innovation.
records.SM_Text:
Dr. Anil Sukhdeorao Bonde:

??????????? There is urgent need to support medical technology innovation through structured policy frameworks such as Research-Linked Incentives (RLIs). As a medical professional. I believe India stands at a defining moment in healthcare transformation. Demographic shifts, digital acceleration, and increasing demand for affordable and high-quality medical technologies require decisive policy interventions.

??????????? While the Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme has supported manufacturing, India still imports over 70% of high-end medical technologies. Significant gaps persist in design-led R&D, clinical validation, IP monetization, and global competitiveness. The National Policy on R&D and Innovation in Pharma-MedTech (2023) is a positive step, but targeted support is needed to realize its vision truly. RLIs provide structured incentives throughout the innovation lifecycle - from prototyping to regulatory approval. A three-tiered framework aligned with Technology Readiness Levels can provide milestone-based grants, co-funded clinical trials in India, and tax benefits on patent royalties. This complements national initiatives, such as the PRIP (Promotion of Research and Innovation in Pharma MedTech Sector) scheme and the Anusandhan National Research Foundation.

Successful R&D-linked incentive models already exist in sectors like semiconductors, EVs, and pharmaceuticals. Globally, countries like the US and Singapore have demonstrated the success of similar frameworks. With Indias MedTech sector projected to grow from $12 billion in 2023 to $50 billion by 2030, we must act now.

??????????? I urge the Government to adopt RLIs and ensure long-term support for MedTech innovation, making "Innovate in India" a practical reality.

(ENDS)

records.subject: Establishing Clinics for Sexual Problems at All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) in India.
records.SM_Text:
Dr. Anil Sukhdeorao Bonde: Sexual health is a fundamental aspect of overall well-being, yet sexual problems in males, including impotency and various sexual disorders, remain significantly prevalent in India. According to studies, approximately 52% of men between 40 to 70 years old experience some form of erectile dysfunction, with the prevalence expected to rise due to lifestyle changes and increasing stress levels. Moreover, the incidence of other sexual disorders like premature ejaculation and low libido is also substantial, affecting the quality of life and mental health of a significant portion of the male population. Unfortunately, a substantial number of affected individuals seek treatment from unqualified practitioners, leading to inadequate and non-evidence-based management. Recognizing the urgency of addressing this issue, we propose the establishment of specialized clinics for sexual problems at all All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) locations across the country. These clinics will adopt a multidisciplinary approach involving urologists, endocrinologists, psychiatrists, and counsellors to provide comprehensive care to patients.

This initiative will not only improve the quality of care but also prevent the exploitation of affected individuals by unqualified practitioners. records.subject: Demand for Production-Linked Incentive Scheme
records.SM_Text:
डा. अनिल सुखदेवराव बोंडे (महाराष्ट्र) : माननीय उपसभापति महोदय, उद्योग जगत में मोदी सरकार ने Production Linked Incentive Scheme लगाकर उद्योग को प्रोत्साहित किया है। मैं मोदी सरकार का अभिनंदन करता हूँ। खेती एक ऐसा उद्योग है जिससे देश की भूख मिटाई जाती है, मानवीय भरण पोषण होता है तथा देश के सकल घरेलू उत्पाद में भी खेती तथा खेती संलग्न व्यवसाय का योगदान है। लेकिन ऐसा अनुभव होता है कि किसान का ज्यादा उत्पादन होता है, तो उसके भाव कम हो जाते हैं। यह बात प्याज, टमाटर, सब्जियों, अनाज, कपास अन्य के बारे में देखी गयी है। किसान मेहनत करके अपनी फसलों का उत्पादन बढ़ाता है। उसके लिए उसे मज़दूरी, तकनीकी, खाद आदि के इस्तेमाल में पैसा खर्च करना पड़ता है, लेकिन उत्पादन बढ़ाने के बाद भी उसका फायदा उसे नहीं मिल पाता है। किसान जितना उत्पादन बढ़ाता है, उतना उसे प्रोत्साहित करना ज़रुरी है।

???? कुछ राज्यों मे धान उत्पादन को प्रोत्साहित करने के लिए बोनस के रूप में एमएसपी से ज्यादा रकम दी जाती है। महाराष्ट्र में सरकार ने भाव कम होने पर प्याज के लिए 200 रुपये प्रति क्विंटल और धान के लिए 15,000 रुपये प्रति हेक्टेयर का प्रोत्साहन दिया था। इसी उपलक्ष्य मे उत्पादन बढ़ाने के लिए एमएसपी से ज्यादा प्रोत्साहन अनुदान देने की ज़रूरत है। इस संदर्भ में कृषि तथा कृषि संलग्न उत्पादों के लिए उत्पादन बढ़ाओ और प्रोत्साहन राशि पाओ, ऐसी योजना पर सरकार विचार करे।

(समाप्त)

records.SM_Text:
डा. अनिल सुखदेवराव बोंडे (महाराष्ट्र) : माननीय उपसभाध्यक्ष जी, मैं आपके माध्यम से सदन का ध्यान विदर्भ संभाग के एक महत्वपूर्ण विषय पर आकृष्ट करते हुए निवेदन करना चाहता हूं कि 8 जुलाई, 2022 के बाद वर्धा एवं अमरावती जिले सहित पूरे विदर्भ में लगातार भारी वर्षा होने के कारण लगभग सभी नदियों एवं उपनदियों में बाढ़ की परिस्थिति निर्मित हुई है। भारी वर्षा एवं बाढ़ के कारण दुर्भाग्यपूर्ण रूप से अनेक सामान्य नागरिकों की मृत्यु हुई है एवं बिजली गिरने के कारण परिसर में जनहानि हुई है। लगातार हुई भारी वर्षा के कारण अनेक जगहों पर आवास क्षतिग्रस्त हुए हैं तथा किसान वर्ग की फसलों को भी भारी नुकसान होने की जानकारी सामने आ रही है।

अत: सदन के माध्यम से मेरा केन्द्रीय गृह मंत्री जी से निवेदन है कि वे इस घटना का संज्ञान लेकर, इस कठिन परिस्थिति में सामान्य नागरिकों तथा किसानों को आवश्यक राहत तथा तत्काल मदद केन्द्र सरकार के माध्यम से मिलने हेतु आवश्यक कार्रवाई कराने की कृपा करें।

??????????????? (समाप्त)
